newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels likely took town in east - officials.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels likely took town in east - officials.

text.p: Zaire defence ministry officials said on Sunday it was likely the eastern town of Kalima, deserted by about 25,000 Hutu refugees, had been overrun by rebels, but they had yet to receive details.

"I was told that the situation at Kalima was worrying and informed that there were rebels advancing on that road," one senior official told Reuters in the capital. "There were only a few Zairean soldiers there so if it has fallen it would not suprise me, but I cannot confirm it."
Earlier missionaries near Kalima, contacted by radio from Rwanda, said they believed the town had fallen to Laurent Kabila's fighters of the Alliance of Democratic Forces.

The rebels, fighting to overthrow Zaire's president of 31 years Mobutu Sese Seko, control a strip of territory over 1,000 km (600 miles) long and have begun to advance deeper towards the heart of the mineral-rich central African country.

The Zaire officials, commenting on the war situation for the first time since U.N. officials reported the mysterious disappearence of the Kalima refugees, signaled a new flareup in the four-month civil war in eastern Zaire.
The frontlines had been relatively quiet since South Africa and regional states launched initiatives last week to try and end the conflict at the negotiating table.
"Our reinforcements are at Kindu where there are even some warplanes, so we can expect a response shortly," the senior official said.

Kalima is about 80 km (50 miles) from Kindu, provincial capital of Maniema. It is one of the main bases in the area for the Zairean military which is struggling to beat back the Tutsi-led rebels who took up arms last October.
